summary: Both draw a hue-cycling comet head chasing round a ring, but the port rotates the wrong way, runs ~2.3x too slow, is ~7x too dim, and renders at native display resolution instead of the original's fixed 8x8 canvas.
observations: Shared concept confirmed on both sides: a single ring (circle) with one bright head and a decaying trail that wraps the whole circumference, hue advancing continuously; both start from a single dot at t=0 and have the trail filled in by ~1.3 s; ring diameter is ~11 px across on the default 16x16 grid on both.

STRUCTURE — the original renders into a FIXED 8x8 logical canvas: in the 16x16 dump every lit feature is an exact 2x2 block (rows and columns duplicated pairwise), and re-rendering on an 8x8 rig gives byte-identical cell values (230,207,49,187,255,11,169,74,152,19,137,82,124,8,91,101,112,7 at t=3.0 in both runs). The port draws in native display coordinates: a 1-px-wide, jagged ring of ~54 lit pixels on 16x16, and a completely different, gappy 10-lit-pixel ring on 8x8. The port's output changes with rig size; the original's does not.

MOTION DIRECTION — opposite. Tracking the peak pixel's angle at 100 fps over t=3.0..3.5 s: original 122->135->148->165->185->204->216->232->276->354->414 deg (monotonically increasing, i.e. head runs upper-left -> left -> bottom -> right); port 255->241->225->209->198->175->162->135 deg (monotonically decreasing, i.e. bottom -> lower-left -> left -> upper-left). Confirmed independently at 40 fps and at the default 20 fps.
MOTION SPEED — original sweeps ~584 deg/s (one lap per ~0.62 s); port sweeps ~240-270 deg/s (one lap per ~1.3-1.5 s). Port is ~2.2-2.4x too slow.

HUE RATE — original's head hue advances ~365 deg/s (orange->yellow->green->cyan across t=3.00..3.375 s); port's advances ~140 deg/s (cyan 196 deg -> blue 220 deg -> violet 245 deg across t=3.00..3.35 s). Same full-saturation rainbow family on both, ~2.5x slower on the port.

BRIGHTNESS — original's head is pinned at value 255 in every frame sampled (t=3.0, 3.5, 40, 41, 42, 43 s); the port's head peak is only ~85-135 at 20 fps and fluctuates frame-to-frame (82,86,105,143,198,169,137,117,221 across 0.02 s steps at 100 fps), so the port also visibly shimmers where the original is rock-steady. Whole-frame lit-pixel sum: original ~7900-8100, port ~1110-1190 (~7x dimmer). meanBrightness over the 60 s survey: orig avg 16.3, port avg 2.0.

The port's low absolute levels make the harness's motion stat read 0 for 282/300 survey frames (sub-quantisation changes); the port is NOT frozen - the dumps show the head advancing - but its 8-bit output is nearly static between adjacent frames.

STEADY STATE — neither side dies. brightnessTrend 'steady' on both over 60 s; a --skip 40 window shows the same behaviour each side had at t=3 s (orig peak 255 / sum ~8000, port peak ~90-120 / sum ~1130).

No regime/mode structure: the only distinct phase is the ~0-1.3 s trail build-up, after which both sides hold one continuous regime for the whole 60 s survey (rhythm waterfalls show uniform blocky banding end to end, no boundaries).
Deterministic: a seed-7 run is pixel-identical to seed 1 on both sides, so no RNG character to judge.
CONTROLS — the probe reports 'no settable controls' on BOTH sides; control surfaces match (both empty).
feedback: Reverse the head's direction of travel: the original's head runs counter-clockwise on screen (upper-left -> left -> bottom -> right); the port runs clockwise.

Slow-motion is the wrong word - the port is too slow. Original completes one lap of the ring in ~0.62 s (~584 deg/s); the port takes ~1.3-1.5 s (~250 deg/s). Speed the port up by ~2.3x. The hue cycle needs the same ~2.5x speed-up (orig ~365 deg of hue per second, port ~140).

Raise brightness by roughly 7x overall. The original's head sits at full value 255 in every frame; the port's peaks at only ~85-135 and its whole-frame lit sum is ~1130 against the original's ~7950. The trail's decay shape is right in character (a smooth ramp wrapping the full ring on both) - it is the absolute level that is wrong.

The defining feature of this pattern is that it draws into a FIXED-SIZE 8x8 canvas and scales that canvas to whatever display it is on: on a 16x16 grid the original's features are exact 2x2 blocks, and the original's 8x8 render is numerically identical to its 16x16 render. The port instead rasterises the ring directly at display resolution, giving a thin 1-px ring on 16x16 and a broken 10-pixel ring on 8x8. Reintroduce the fixed 8x8 canvas + upscale so the port is resolution-independent and its features come out chunky.

Once the canvas is fixed-resolution, the head-brightness shimmer should go away too: the original's head lands squarely on one 8x8 cell at full 255 every frame, while the port's sub-pixel head splits energy between neighbouring pixels and its peak swings between ~80 and ~220 within a fifth of a second.
